title: Lighthouse Industries on-prem capacity, upgrade & TF playbook (draft)
content:
Overview:
This is a working draft for Lighthouse Industries' private deployment (VPC + on-prem appliance) sizing, Terraform module notes, and the upgrade/rollback playbook. Primary goals: predictable 99th percentile latency under 450ms for 512-token generations, capacity to handle steady-state throughput of 180 req/s (avg payload 350 tokens), and a safe upgrade path from current runtime v1.10 -> v1.14 with zero data exfil risk and minimal downtime.

Key customer context and constraints:
- Customer: Lighthouse Industries (manufacturing analytics, PCI-adjacent data).
- Must run inside customer VPC with no egress to public internet except to Redwood control-plane endpoints (allowlisted IPs).
- KMS integration required for model keys (AWS KMS + customer HSM) and audit logs must be forwarded to customer SIEM.
- Planned initial fleet: 6 inference nodes (on-prem appliances) + 2 control-plane VMs in their colo (for private control plane).
- Expected peak QPS: 400 small requests/minute burstable (approx 6.7 rps) to larger analytic jobs; steady-state 180 req/s as above.
- Max sequence length: 2048 tokens for few-shot pipelines; average KV cache reuse high (prefix-heavy).
- Customer will provide 40GbE switching and IPsec tunnels to our control plane.

Sizing assumptions (working):
- Model: OpenModelX-13B quantized (q4) memory footprint per replica: ~35GB.
- Node spec (appliance): 4 x A800 GPUs (80 GB GPU VRAM total), 512 GB system RAM, 24 cores CPU, NVMe 4TB.
- Replica packing: 1x model replica per GPU to maintain KV cache locality and avoid cross-GPU sharding complexity.
- Target throughput per node: 110–140 tokens/sec (depending on sequence length). With 6 nodes -> estimated capacity: 660–840 tokens/sec which maps to ~200–250 512-token requests/sec at optimistic batching. We conservatively size for 180 req/s.
- Autoscaling: vertical scaling via adding profile to TF modules is manual for on-prem; we set a surge pool of 1 warm node for maintenance/failover.

Networking and security (requirements + config notes):
- Subnets: Control-plane subnets (private) and inference subnet (isolated).
- IPsec: Use customer-managed IPsec; verify MTU (jumbo frames disabled).
- Firewall: Only allow control-plane port 443 to Redwood endpoints and SSH from customer infra for troubleshooting (jumpbox).
- Egress: Block all egress except to Redwood allowlist endpoints and KMS endpoints.
- Certificates: Mutual TLS for control-plane <-> agent; we will provide CSR flow to customer CA.

Terraform module notes (high-level):
- We will reuse modules: redwood/vpc-peering, redwood/onprem-appliance, redwood/kms-integration.
- Customer wants their terraform to manage networking and our modules to be included as a submodule. We will produce a small wrapper module 'redwood/lighthouse-wrapper' that pins versions and hides infra details.
- Important variables to expose to customer: appliance_count, appliance_profile (gpu_count), allowed_controlplane_cidrs, kms_key_arn, bootstrap_token_ttl_hours.
- State: remote backend must be S3 with encryption and state_lock via DynamoDB (customer AWS account). We will provide sample backend.tf.

Suggested Terraform snippet (example wrapper usage):

module "redwood_lighthouse" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules//lighthouse-wrapper"
  appliance_count = 6
  appliance_profile = "a800-4g"
  allowed_controlplane_cidrs = ["10.18.0.0/28"]
  kms_key_arn = "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh"
  bootstrap_token = "${var.bootstrap_token}"
}

Notes on TF upgrade practices:
- Modules are versioned using tags; we will create a release tag v2025.02.lighthouse for any changes.
- Upgrade plan: bump module tag in wrapper, run terraform plan, and only apply on staging customer account first (2 node replica). We will perform a canary rollout.

Upgrade/Canary plan (v1.10 -> v1.14):
1) Prep: backup control-plane DB snapshot (customer-managed), snapshot appliance NVMe, export current TF state and record commit hash.
2) Staging canary: deploy new runtime v1.14 on 1 appliance in customer staging VLAN with same config. Run regression suite (see test list below).
3) Canary validation (48 hours): monitor latency, tail latency, token cost, and quality checks on a set of 120 eval prompts (customer provided). Automatic rollback if 99th pct latency increases by >15% or quality metric drop >2% (per eval).
4) Gradual rollout: replace appliances in batches of 2 nodes. Maintain at least N-2 capacity during each batch. Pause and run smoke tests between batches.
5) Post-upgrade: run full traffic replay overnight and keep enhanced observability (retain increased sampling for 72 hours).
6) Rollback: If rollback needed, revert module tag and runtime container image, and use snapshot to restore NVMe cache.

Validation test list (staging must pass):
- 60-minute steady-state 180 req/s replay with mixed sequences (32–2048 tokens).
- 1-hour burst test: synthetic spiky traffic (4x expected) to test queueing/backpressure.
- KV cache correctness check: validated outputs for 200 prefix cases.
- KMS/HSM signing verification for model key operations.
- SIEM log ingestion verification (customer endpoint).

Open questions / Risks (to resolve with customer):
- HSM pairing: does customer require on-prem HSM? If yes, timeline and cert exchange steps.
- Network route priority: will customer accept BGP peering or only static tunnels? BGP would simplify failover.
- Rack-level cooling and power redundancy: appliance spec requires dual power feeds for SLA; confirmation needed.
- Disaster recovery RTO/RPO expectations beyond planned surge pool.
- Legal/compliance: are there additional logging retention rules in their APAC operations?

Runbook excerpts (failure scenarios):
- Node GPU OOM during inference: immediate action: drain node (TF reprovision), switch routing to warm node, capture kernel logs / nvidia-smi output, escalate to runtime team.
- Control-plane unreachable: fallback to local agent mode (read-only serving) for up to 6 hours; alert SRE + customer ops; attempt re-establish IPsec; if unrecoverable, follow emergency rollback to previous runtime image.
- KMS unavailable: degrade to cached model keys for 15 minutes (cached keys TTL), after TTL start rejecting new model loads and alerting security.

Operational tasks and owner matrix (high level):
- Redwood infra: provide wrapper TF module, runtime images, canary plan, and observability dashboards. Owner: Ravi Kapoor.
- Customer infra: provide VPC/subnets, S3 + DynamoDB for TF state, and KMS/HSM. Owner: Lighthouse cloud ops.
- Redwood SRE: run upgrade and be on-call for the 72-hour post-upgrade window. Owner: Ethan Morales.

Deliverables and timeline (proposed):
- Week 0: finalize appliance spec, network details, and signing cert exchange.
- Week 1: deliver wrapper TF module and sample backend.tf; customer test apply in staging.
- Week 2: staging canary run and validation.
- Week 3: production rollout (batch windows scheduled with customer maintenance windows).

Action items (next steps):
- [Sana] Schedule technical deep-dive with Lighthouse networking team (ASAP).
- [Ethan] Prepare runtime v1.14 canary image and smoke test harness.
- [Ravi] Draft wrapper TF module and verify S3 backend config with customer.
- [Customer] Confirm HSM requirement and power redundancy in colocation.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider an optional tiny control-plane fallback in customer account (managed by Redwood) for faster failover. Need legal sign-off.
- Keep TF variables minimal; push complexity into module defaults.
- Add a smoke endpoint for quick synthetic checks that only returns health metrics (no PII).

References and artifacts:
- TF modules repo: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules (see PR #87 for onprem appliances).
- Canary test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/canary-tests/tree/lighthouse
- Compliance checklist: confluence.redwood/lighthouse-onprem-reqs

Unresolved items to capture in the customer kickoff:
1) IP ranges for control plane allowlist (customer to provide).
2) Exact SLAs for node-level replacement (target 4-hour replacement).
3) Confirmation on log forwarding retention window.

This doc is a working draft—expect lots of followups after the architectural kick-off. Keep comments inline in this doc and we will iterate toward a final playbook for the execution runbook and the TF module release notes.
